sentences.text: Portugalosuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliform.
The type species of the genus is Portugalosuchus azenhae.
Portugalosuchus is classified within the family Gavialidae.
If classified as a basal crocodylian, Portugalosuchus would be the oldest known crocodylian.
A 2021 study placed Portugalosuchus within Crocodylia as a member of Gavialidae closely related to thoracosaurs like Thoracosaurus.
Portugalosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Fossils of this animal date from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
The only known fossils come from the Tentugal Formation in Portugal.
Researchers have noted that Portugalosuchus might possibly fall outside of Crocodylia entirely.
A 2022 analysis using morphological and DNA data suggested Portugalosuchus is outside Crocodylia as the sister taxon to Allodaposuchidae.
